lead: the one signed page in your life sits in a drawer at home, and everything you have ever made went out into the world without so much as a sentence attached to it.
sun: work leaves your hands finished and bare — no conditions, nothing written down about what happens to it afterwards — and because it is good it gets handled constantly, by people who take a thing this well made to be somebody's business to look after. the only undertaking you have ever put in writing is the one you gave at the beginning of a marriage, and it covers a household, not a workshop.
moon: The Crown entered that one on purpose — a plain sentence said once, with decades folded into it — and it has held since without maintenance. the terms were set by someone who owned nothing and they oblige someone who owns something: a household this size runs on finished work leaving at a rate, so what the vow means in practice is that the pieces keep going out.
pull: a promise you made once has held for twenty-five years without being looked at again. the work goes out under no promise, and the people who take it have watched how you keep one.
tension: you get asked to hold things — executor, witness, the person who keeps the second copy — because a word that visibly survives decades is what a family reaches for, and you are good at it. nobody has ever asked whether anything of yours is held. one arrangement that steady reads as a life with its affairs in order, so the workshop is assumed to be covered by something of the same kind, and it is covered by nothing.
cost: an undertaking given at twenty-six is still exactly that undertaking at fifty, unrevised and uncomplained about, and whole structures get built on top of it — a family, two businesses, an estate somebody left in your keeping. the same steadiness pointed at a made thing would have taken one clause at the start. the pieces are correctly credited everywhere and belong, in practice, to whoever has them.

lead: there is a date and anyone can check it. you did this before anybody, everyone doing it now learned it from a piece that carries your name, and nothing in the field sits above you.
sun: the rank rests on something checkable — an object with a date on it, your name spelled correctly on the earliest copy, no argument possible about who made it. it was also unfenced from the hour it appeared. no condition was ever written about who could use it or how, so the thing spread the same season into hands you have not met, and the spreading is what made you senior in the trade.
moon: seniority arrived early here and nobody offered it. one year the hard questions began coming to you and they have not stopped. there is no one above you, which means nowhere to bring a thing. when a younger maker lifts the piece whole and puts a new name beside yours, the objection gets made downward, from the top of a trade, at somebody holding nothing.
pull: every dispute in this trade comes to you to be settled. the one that is yours has nowhere to go, because anything said from up here arrives as a ruling rather than a grievance.
tension: the deference is total and it converts whatever you say into policy. mention mildly, at a table, that someone has used the piece oddly, and within a week that person's funding is uncertain and three people write to say they took your point. so you stop mentioning it. the quiet gets read as stature, a senior person declining to bother with small things, and every year of it makes that reading firmer.
cost: nothing you assert about the technique has to be argued down. the record closes in one sentence what would take somebody else a decade, the whole trade uses that, and it is why the difficult questions arrive here at all. the rank has one motion it cannot make. wanting a thing back reads, from this height, as taking it off somebody smaller, and everyone would say so kindly.

lead: you went down looking for where your own best piece came from, past the story everyone tells about it, and you found the man it actually came from. then you published that, entire.
sun: the making has never been in question and nobody disputes it now. what stood undefended was the account of where it began — flattering, roughly accurate, and doing real work in front of the object every time a hostile reader came near. you took that down yourself, at full length, in public, because a finished finding leaves your hands the same way a finished piece does: complete, attributed, with nothing over it.
moon: The Root goes under the plausible causes. there were three, any of them publishable, and beneath all of them sat the actual one — an unread ledger, a dead man's margins, a date that fits nobody's story. by the second month you could see what the finding would do to your own standing, and nothing in you issues the ruling that a thing has been understood well enough already.
pull: the account that protected your best piece was dismantled from the inside. the sentence that now reduces the work is one nobody else had to dig for. you did the digging and published it.
tension: inside a year the correction became the interesting fact about you, repeated at introductions ahead of the piece it concerns, which reads as a footnote now. people cite it warmly, as proof of a rare honesty, then put it to uses of their own. the digging has not stopped either — two colleagues' origin stories, the founding account of the discipline, all of it accurate and published bare, and each of those people carries a version of you now.
cost: people bring you the account nobody else could break, because you broke your own first and did it where everyone could watch, and the findings hold up decades later. what came up out of your own ground is the summary of you now. nothing puts it back. the story that stood between the work and a hostile reader was true enough, and you are the one who removed it.

lead: the hall split last year and both halves walked out with the thing you made — one object, one name on it, going in two directions carried by people who no longer speak to each other.
sun: the thing that held that crowd together is an object, and everyone knows whose it is: sung, printed, hung at the front, credited every time it gets used. it went to the room outright, the way everything of yours goes out, with no membership condition on it and no sentence anywhere about what happens if the room stops being one room. when the room stopped being one room, it went with both.
moon: you could see the body separating a season before it separated — who was arriving, who had already left in their head, which sentence at which meeting decided it. The Flock hands you that reading about a crowd that was never yours to sort, and you have been in the hall twenty years without once standing in the middle of it, so both halves are certain you are theirs.
pull: both congregations use it, and each is sure the maker is with them. you saw the separation coming a season out, told nobody, and made the thing they would each need to take.
tension: each side invites you to speak now, and the invitation is to authenticate — the maker in the room means the room is the real one. refusing both would be a verdict. attending both reads as somebody standing above the argument, and that reading is warm and wrong, since what happens is that you hear the accurate part of each case and have no apparatus for choosing. you get quoted by people whose reasons you would not sign.
cost: a room tells you months ahead who is leaving, and you make things that will still work for whoever remains, which is why what comes off your table outlives the body it was made for. that sorting never gets pointed at your own holdings. the object travels with the people, in every direction at once, and each faction is satisfied that it has the original.
